vaasa-ojen-nature-trail.desc:
Öjen is an unusually large old-growth forest reserve for western Finland (old-growth forest protection programme and Natura 2000), managed by Metsähallitus. Most of the area is old, spruce-dominated conifer forest, partly paludified; the oldest trees are nearly 200 years old. Along the loop the landscape varies from lush shore groves to barren rocky pine forest on bedrock, on gently undulating terrain with duckboards that can be slippery.

Info boards present the forest nature, medicinal plants and old folk beliefs. On Kompassberget, the highest point, two stone compass roses mark the cardinal directions. Rest site with benches, campfire place (bring own firewood) and composting toilet.
vaasa-ojen-nature-trail.duration: 2.5–3 h on foot. 4.5 km loop; about 5.7–5.9 km including the ~0.6 km approach from the parking each way.
parking_notes: Parking on Myrgrundintie (road 6741); walk ~300 m along the gravel road Öjenintie to a small bridge and info boards on the left.

vaasa-riso-trail.desc:
The trail circles the Risöfladan area at the inner end of the Eteläinen Kaupunginselkä (Southern City Bay), one of Finland's best wetland bird sites, on state land by the reed-fringed estuary of the Tuovila/Laihia river. The loop is easy gravel road (also cyclable); the spur to the Ryövärinkari bird tower is a duckboard path through forest and reedbed that can be partly under water at high sea level.

In spring and autumn migration hundreds of geese, swans and waders and thousands of waterfowl rest and feed here; reedbeds hold reed bunting, sedge warbler and bearded tit. Campfire place and dry toilet by the tower; a second, lower viewing platform lies at the river mouth.
highlights: Ryövärinkari bird tower (closed since 23.10.2025 due to rot damage)
vaasa-riso-trail.network_note: ~3.6 km gravel-road loop with spur paths to the Ryövärinkari (Rövarskäret) bird tower (~350 m duckboard path) and the Risö viewing platform; about 4.9 km with the spurs.
vaasa-riso-trail.season: No winter maintenance. Ryövärinkari bird tower closed since 23 Oct 2025 (rot damage); the viewing platform is open. Duckboards may flood at high water.
parking_notes: Risö parking area at the end of Ampujantie, south of the motorway.

vaasa-ojberget-nature-trail.desc:
Öjberget is part of a rocky forested ridge rising from the fields of Sundom, about 270 ha of mainly pine–lingonberry heath forest, bordering the Söderfjärden meteorite crater (c. 520 million years old) to the south. The trail runs from the Öjbergsmossen bog past a giant's kettle (pothole) and across a boulder field ('devil's field') to the stunted pines on the crater rim.

The area holds the oldest traces of human activity in the Vaasa region, a Stone Age site c. 4,000 years old. The lookout tower on the ski-slope top (65 m a.s.l.) views Söderfjärden, the archipelago and Vaasa; owls call in late winter. Fitness stairs (271 steps) lead down to the stadium and grill hut.
vaasa-ojberget-nature-trail.duration: At least 1.5 h; shorter 2 km yellow-marked variant from Markenintie.
parking_notes: Öjberget winter sports centre / stadium area; the trail starts at the large info board by the ski lodge.

vaasa-pilvilampi-network.desc:
Pilvilampi lies 9 km east of the centre on the Höstvesi ridge, a large upland that continues north beyond the city. The ~800 ha forest is mostly very bouldery and partly rough going, with patches of old spruce forest among younger conifers and extensive lily-of-the-valley carpets under the spruces. The lake is a raw-water reservoir (no swimming or dogs in the water).

Nesting waterfowl include goldeneye, tufted duck and common sandpiper; forests hold hazel grouse, black grouse, pygmy owl, black woodpecker and long-tailed tit. Many shelters: Närvänmutka, Käpykota, Kivijärvi and Aurinko lean-tos, Eetun piilo, Kuutamo and Höstvesi lean-tos, Pilvimaja cabin, plus viewpoints.

Near the southern end of the lake are two protected ancient monuments: in the shore water, next to a boulder, a flat stone with the year 1589 carved into one corner (at times under water, as the lake level is regulated), and about 450 m to the south, on a hill between Pilvilampi and the drained Skomakarträsket, the stone foundations of old buildings, one stone bearing the year 1604. Viking Age objects have been found nearby by metal detecting.
highlights: stones carved with the years 1589 and 1604
vaasa-pilvilampi-network.network_note: Extensive network of marked paths and forest roads over an ~800 ha area (~4 × 4 km) around Pilvilampi lake, linked to Vaasa's 70 km outdoor trail system. Sensible rounds: lake loop ~3–5 km; longer rounds via Kivijärvi and Pilvimaja ~10–12 km.
vaasa-pilvilampi-network.access: Easy to reach by Vaasa city buses (Vaasa local transport, journey planner: https://vaasa.digitransit.fi/).
vaasa-pilvilampi-network.season: Ski tracks in winter (Vaasan Latu); 22 km winter fatbike trail.
parking_notes: Main Pilvilampi parking by the start of the trails (Kappelinmäentie).
Gädda ski-track parking ('Latuparkki') at the north-west trailhead.
South trailhead by the forest road; exact address uncertain.

vaasa-city-bay-trail.desc:
A mostly accessible shore path following the Eteläinen Kaupunginselkä (Southern City Bay), a 6 km long sea bay narrowing towards the Tuovila/Laihia river delta. It goes around the Brage open-air museum and Emäntälahti bay in Hietalahti and Suvilahti, through lush deciduous shore groves (aspens used by flying squirrels, old villa-garden plants), past shallow bays and new islets rising through land uplift, then the Old Vaasa canal and Majakkakivi beacon boulder, ending at the Natura 2000 reedbeds near Risö.

Sixteen signs present history and nature (bats, moor frog, birds, land uplift). Grebes, ducks, geese and waders gather in migration; thrush nightingales sing in the groves. Rest and campfire sites, beaches and a parallel canoe route.
vaasa-city-bay-trail.duration: Kalaranta–Majakkakivi 7 km; continues ~3 km to Risö (one way). First section of a planned ~30 km round of the Southern City Bay.
vaasa-city-bay-trail.access: Easy to reach by Vaasa city buses (Vaasa local transport, journey planner: https://vaasa.digitransit.fi/).
parking_notes: Start at Kalaranta on the city-centre shore; public parking also at Hietalahti and Suvilahti, and the east end connects to Risö parking (Ampujantie).

vahakyro-ojaniemi-hyyria.desc:
Paths wind through the forests of Ojaniemi and Hyyriä villages, mostly fresh and dry heath forest, with herb-rich vegetation and the Vainionperä spring near the start. Palolampi pond has a bird tower; Palanusenkallio's folded bedrock ridges show post-glacial changes and the Ojaniemi lean-to (fireplace, toilet, overnight use) stands on top.

The Marjamäki route follows rocky ridges unusual for Vähäkyrö and passes Iron Age (c. 400–800 AD) burial cairns at Marjamäki and Huumansaari, plus Kylymä helevetti ('cold hell' in the local dialect), a hiding place from the Great Northern War. The children's trail has animal-themed boards.
vahakyro-ojaniemi-hyyria.network_note: Colour-coded routes of 1.4–11.7 km from two trailheads. From Hyyriäntie 105: Children's trail 2.1 km, Palolampi 2.1 km, Palanusenkallio 1.4 km, Hyyriä 4.4 km and Marjamäki 11.7 km. From Kaitaja parking (Hyyriäntie 478): Kylymä helevetti round 2.7 km.
vahakyro-ojaniemi-hyyria.season: No winter maintenance. Mountain biking allowed (partly very hard).
parking_notes: Main trailhead, room for 8 cars, info board.
Kaitaja parking (2–3 cars) for the Kylymä helevetti round; road use restricted during farm work.

vahakyro-kruutari-mestoosplassi.desc:
Easy routes mostly on old cart tracks, forest paths and tractor tracks through Ostrobothnian field and barn landscape and forest, with stony sections mid-way on the Klapurintönkkä path. Good spots for watching spring and autumn bird migration over the fields; several old springs (Heininniemenmäki spring) and the Haarajoki stream.

The Kruutari and Klapurintönkkä paths pass Iron Age (Merovingian, c. 400–800 AD) cairns of the Vallinmäki settlement unit. Mestoosplassi is a former execution site (late 1500s–1825) with an info board. Haarajoki and Selkämäki lean-tos have fireplaces, toilets and firewood.
vahakyro-kruutari-mestoosplassi.network_note: 5 loop and linear routes of 2.6–8.4 km from two trailheads. From Kruutarinmaja: Kruutari loop 2.6 km, Klapurintönkkä path 3–8.4 km (linear to Perkiöntie), Heininniemenmäki loop 6.2 km. From Mestoosplassi: Niisneva loop 3.4 km, Koirasaari route 7.4 km.
vahakyro-kruutari-mestoosplassi.season: No winter maintenance. Signposted links to Ojaniemi–Hyyriä network.
parking_notes: Kruutarinmaja (Kruutari house), info board.
Mestoosplassi, info board.

vahakyro-saarenpaa-mullola.desc:
A loop on village roads and cart tracks through traditional Kyrö river farmland and forest, with short spurs to sights. Along Ainmaantie are Iron Age burial cairns, springs (Jaakob's spring), the 'shepherd's writing stone' and Jätintie, a 49 m stone-slab causeway over 1,400 years old, regarded as Finland's oldest stone bridge, built over a former wetland when sea level was higher.

Further on: forest-workers' camp sites, the Kylymä helevetti hiding place, Kaitaja lean-to and viewpoint, the site of Mullovius parsonage and the ancient Mullola harbour (a reminder of land uplift), and two rock-carved sundials.
vahakyro-saarenpaa-mullola.duration: Main loop ~14 km (anticlockwise); ~21 km with all out-and-back spurs to sights. Recommended by bike, spurs on foot.
vahakyro-saarenpaa-mullola.season: No winter maintenance. Avoid driving the narrow cart roads during farm work; Savisilta hut: avoid during moose hunting.
parking_notes: Saarenpää sports lodge yard; Saarenpää lean-to and info board behind the lodge.

vahakyro-petulian-patikka.desc:
The trail explores Aittoomäki, the 'seven hills' area nicknamed Petulia city, which was an important Iron Age dwelling and probably trading place when the Kyrönjoki river mouth lay at Tervajoki around the start of the Common Era. Over a hundred burial cairns and about ten dwelling sites are known; settlement moved on as land uplift pushed the shore away. Signposted spurs lead to cairns at Aittoomäki and Höysälänmäki.

Road sections cross open Ostrobothnian fields; forest paths are stony and partly wet. Boards present forest nature (kettle hole, flying squirrel, Höysälänlakia birds, Turukivi boulder). Lean-to with fireplace and toilet at Hirsikorpi.
vahakyro-petulian-patikka.network_note: Main loop 7.8 km (anticlockwise) + spurs (total 10.1 km). Short options from Hirsikorpi hunting lodge: ~2 km loop to the kettle hole and ~1 km linear to Turukivi.
vahakyro-petulian-patikka.season: No winter maintenance, no firewood service. Avoid during hunting season.
parking_notes: Junction of Kyröntie (highway 18) and Aittoomäentie, info board.
Hirsikorpi hunting lodge yard (lean-to); start for the short loops.

vahakyro-kolkki-nature-trail.desc:
A short trail by the Kyrönjoki river right next to the Kolkinkoski rapids, using old paths of the former Kolkki sawmill and cloth-mill site and new wood-chip sections. It loops around Kolkki manor (one of Vaasa's oldest buildings), Vartiosaari and Kuljunsaari islands within a nationally significant built cultural environment (RKY), with history boards.

The Vartiosaari path runs close to the river at the southern tip (take care). Vartiosaari lean-to with campfire and fishing spot by the rapids; firewood and fishing permits from Kolkki manor.
vahakyro-kolkki-nature-trail.network_note: Parts: Vartiosaari path 0.5 km, Lyra path 0.7 km; anticlockwise.
vahakyro-kolkki-nature-trail.season: No winter maintenance. Partly runs through a private restaurant's yard area.
parking_notes: Trailhead parking with info board (also start of the Five Bridges cycling route).

vahakyro-korkiavuori.desc: A short forest loop on Korkiavuori hill near Hiiripelto village, one of the five planned Vähäkyrö trail networks. It passes the Ristimäki burial cairn, where a National Board of Antiquities board describes the wealthy Migration and Merovingian period settlement (400–800 AD) and a wine ladle made in Capua, Italy, around 100 AD, found at nearby Kirstintönkkä. The Hauksalo hut of Hiiripelto village (code-locked) lies about 1 km south.
vahakyro-korkiavuori.season: Newer route; signposting may still be incomplete.
parking_notes: Trailhead parking off Kalsilantie; exact address uncertain.

bjorko-panike-trail.desc:
The trail crosses the heart of the Kvarken Archipelago World Heritage Site: land-uplift shores, bays turning into flads and gloe lakes, ponds and small bogs, and grazed birch woods rich in windthrows and hollow trees. From Svedjehamn it passes the Saltkaret tower and the Märaryggbro fish-watching bridge, then becomes a narrow stony path to the Långgrund pier.

A small ferry crosses to Stora Segelsören; the route continues over bridged islands (Slåttskäret, Bullerskäret, Rönnskäret) with sheep pastures, old hay barns and lily-of-the-valley rich uplift forest to Rotörskatan. Shelters, cooking huts and lean-tos along the way.
bjorko-panike-trail.duration: One way: mainland section Svedjehamn–Långgrund pier 3.4 km (7 km return, with a small loop near Långgrund); Svedjehamn–Rotörskatan via the islands c. 12 km. Can be done as a c. 15 km round trip back to Svedjehamn via the southern (wet) branch. With all branches and the Vargis trails on Panike about 23 km (2 days).
bjorko-panike-trail.warning: The islands are reached on a small unmanned cable ferry from Långgrund pier to Stora Segelsören that hikers operate themselves (age 15+, electronic ID required); in 2026 it ran 10–18 daily 15 Jun–16 Aug and at weekends 2 May–14 Jun and 17 Aug–27 Sep, and not at all in strong wind or very low water, so if it is not running turn back at Långgrund and be back at the ferry before 18:00. Continuing from Rotörskatan to Vargis on Panike needs a boat booked in advance (see the boat services listed on the trail's luontoon.fi page); without one you must walk back to Svedjehamn.
bjorko-panike-trail.access: Start at Svedjehamn in Björköby; the mainland section to Långgrund pier needs no crossing.
bjorko-panike-trail.season: No winter maintenance. Sheep grazing June–October. Mosquitoes in summer; stony and wet terrain.
parking_notes: Svedjehamn parking (fee: 2 EUR/4 h, 4 EUR/24 h).
Vargis parking at the Panike end, behind an unlocked barrier (close it after you).

bodvattnet-runt.desc:
An easy loop around Bodvattnet, a former sea bay now almost cut off by land uplift, in the Kvarken World Heritage Site. The path runs on land-uplift shores and through grazed knotty birch woods and moist hollows; Highland cattle graze the shore meadows in summer and many birds nest and rest on the shores.

The 20+ m Saltkaret tower gives a view over the stony archipelago and the "washboard" de Geer moraines; the Märaryggbro bridge is good for watching spawning pike and perch in spring. Bodback, the old fishing harbour from which mail boats rowed to Umeå, is now a museum area with boathouses.
bodvattnet-runt.duration: About 1.5 h. Accessible out-and-back to Saltkaret tower and Bodback c. 3.3 km.
bodvattnet-runt.season: No winter maintenance except parking–tower section. Saltkaret tower open year round.
parking_notes: Svedjehamn parking (fee: 2 EUR/4 h, 4 EUR/24 h).

vikarskat-hamnbastun.desc: Unmaintained shoreline path from Vikarskat fishing harbour along the coast to the harbour sauna at Finnhamnen, in the Kvarken World Heritage archipelago. It passes old-growth forest and gloe lakes formed by land uplift, with sea views, "Russian ovens" (stone-built ovens) and monuments.
vikarskat-hamnbastun.duration: 5 km return (out-and-back to the harbour sauna at Finnhamnen).
parking_notes: Vikarskat fishing harbour (Björköby fiskehamn).

kikanberget.desc: A short unmarked path from Klobbskat at the western tip of Replot up the rocky Kikanberget hill with a Metsähallitus observation tower overlooking the outer Kvarken archipelago and the open sea toward Sweden. Part of the Kvarken World Heritage landscape of moraine islands and rocky shores.
parking_notes: Café Compass parking.

vargis-trails.desc:
Two loops from the old Warg farmstead on Panike, where Richard Warg smuggled liquor during prohibition. Wargrundan (0.8 km) crosses former fields now reforested and has a bench overlooking the Kvicksund strait. Älgrundan (2.6 km) follows the rocky, bouldery shore of Kvicksund, then enters birch woods and old spruce forest.

It passes a boulder field ("devil's field", an ancient shoreline) with a large prehistoric cairn and a viewing platform over Kvicksund and the sea. Big glacial erratics along both paths. Terrain rocky and slippery in places.
parking_notes: Vargis parking at the end of Vargisvägen, behind a barrier on a private road (close it after you). The barrier may be locked outside the summer season; then park at the Panikevägen–Vargisvägen junction and walk the rest.

sommaro-nature-trails.desc:
Trails on the Sommarö headland in the Kvarken World Heritage area, site of a coastal artillery fort (1939–1987) whose bunkers and gun platforms remain. The Ängesholm loop circles a pond in old spruce forest and descends to the shore; the Hålören headland loop has a viewpoint and an accessible viewing platform.

The path also crosses bare rock areas, young aspen stands and a small bog hollow. The longer branch to Sommarösund beach passes a pothole (giant's kettle) and archipelago cultural landscape with stone walls and cairns.
sommaro-nature-trails.duration: Ängesholm loop 1.5 km; Hålören accessible route 2.2 km (out-and-back with 0.8 km loop); linear branch to Sommarösund beach c. 3.4 km one-way (c. 7 km return). Whole network c. 5–8 km.
parking_notes: Public car park at the end of the road near the Sommarö guard hut; the neighbouring lot is private.
Alternative start at Sommarösund beach (Södra Vallgrund); exact address uncertain.

valsorarna-nature-trail.desc:
Remote islands in the outer Kvarken archipelago c. 15 km NW of Björköby. The stony path between the sea rescue station on Ebbskär and the lighthouse on Storskär crosses fragrant heath, rocky shores and flads, with ribbed (Rogen-type) moraines typical of the World Heritage area.

Landmarks are the 36 m red iron lighthouse (1886, built in Paris by the Eiffel Tower firm), keepers' buildings, fishing huts and a monument to Russian soldiers. A biological station (since 1966) serves bird and bat research; white-tailed eagles are common.
valsorarna-nature-trail.warning: Valsörarna can only be reached by boat across open sea: your own boat, a water taxi or a summer excursion boat (e.g. from Björköby or Vaasa), arranged in advance. In summer there are typically one or two scheduled excursions from Svedjehamn; otherwise there is no scheduled service, so agree the pick-up time before you go and allow for wind, which can cancel boat trips.
valsorarna-nature-trail.access: No road access or parking; the islands lie c. 15 km offshore from Björköby. The path runs from the Ebbskär harbour to the lighthouse on Storskär.
valsorarna-nature-trail.season: Landing ban 1 May–31 July (nesting season) except harbours and the nature trail. No winter maintenance.

iskmo-jungsund-trail.desc:
A village-built trail through a string of lakes and flads (land-uplift lagoons) and varied forest north of Jungsund: hills, paths on duckboards over wetlands, blueberry and raspberry patches. Hallonnäsfladan is a highlight; a new observation tower over it opened in October 2026.

Björnhällorna, a scenic rock outcrop with a lean-to, is the most visited rest stop; Kråknäs has a rest area with a bridge over Skatasund. White-tailed eagle, osprey, nesting swans and spring smew can be seen.
iskmo-jungsund-trail.duration: Jungsund–Strömssund 2 km, Strömssund–Hallonnäs 2 km, Hallonnäs–Björnhällorna 2.3 km; Hallonnäsrundan loop 1.8 km, Björnhällsrundan loop 4 km; whole trail 12 km. Må bra-stigen (wellbeing path, blue hearts) = two loops from Hallonnäs, 4 km.
parking_notes: Hallonnäs P1, main parking for the short loops.
Jungsund sports field, southern start.

kunileden.desc:
Loop trail south of Kuni village through forested, hilly terrain with rocky and boulder-strewn areas, small bogs and ditched wetlands. Sights include a small cave ("Grotta") and the bedrock hill Märkenkall (Merkkikallio) at the southern end, with a lean-to and fireplace.

An accessible grill site lies at the Bastuholmsvägen–Kåtakärrvägen junction after 2 km; forest roads allow shortcuts.
kunileden.duration: Northern loop 6.4 km, southern loop 7.9 km (from rest stop 1), whole trail 12.5 km.
parking_notes: Trailhead with info board.

stundars-trails.desc: Marked trails starting from the Stundars open-air museum in Solf, running through forest and field edges west of the museum toward the low-lying farmland near Söderfjärden. The longer 6.6 km route passes a dam and the pumping-station museum; a bird tower at the pumping station overlooks the fields and wetlands. A shorter c. 2 km loop is also signposted on site, but it is not drawn on the map. Info boards along the way.
parking_notes: Stundars museum parking.

skatila-trail.desc: Mostly a forest path of varying width from Skatila sports field westward to Storhälleberget, a bare bedrock hill with a fireplace and views over the surrounding forests of eastern Korsholm. The trail connects to the Pilvilampi trail network and effectively extends it on the eastern side.
parking_notes: Skatila sports field / sports cabin; exact address uncertain.

malsorleden.desc: Forest trail at Mälsor near the Mälsorfjärden bay with sights such as Storstenen (a large glacial erratic, with rest stop), the "Blysten" stone, and the 1958 crash site of a Fokker C.X military aircraft. Moomin figures along the path make it child-friendly; the southern part is marked for dark-season walks with headlamps.
malsorleden.duration: Whole trail c. 9 km; shorter options are a 2.6 km and a 5.2 km loop plus a 0.9 km spur.
parking_notes: Small car park (3 cars).
North parking; exact address uncertain.

tolby-kyrkstigen.desc: Historic church path north from Tölby through Västerskogen, a forest with small bogs and the Västerträsket pond area, to Västernäsbacken by Löjnviken. Beyond lies the flat drained farmland of Risöfladan, a former sea bay, and the pumping station at the Toby river (Laihianjoki) mouth.
tolby-kyrkstigen.duration: 2.1 km to the grill site at Västernäset; +750 m to the pumping station; return by road through Vikby makes a 3.6 km round.
parking_notes: No dedicated parking; park at the roadside near the start.

karikaleden.desc: Trail from Österhankmo beach over bare granite bedrock with lichen-covered rock and open pine forest. A red-marked path leads 0.8 km to Karikaberget, where a 13 m wooden observation tower stands by a fireplace. North of the tower a yellow loop (c. 1.2 km) continues through the bedrock pine forest, and blue and green paths lead further east, returning to the start along the forest road – about 3.4 km as a full round. Walk it as an out-and-back to the tower or as a loop.
karikaleden.duration: Out and back to the tower 1.6 km; the yellow loop north of the tower adds c. 1.2 km; full round via the eastern paths and the forest road c. 3.4 km.
parking_notes: Österhankmo beach.

petsmo-trail.desc:
Varied trail with bogs, old-growth forest and a chain of small, deep lakes (Särkiträsk, Rudträsk, Kvarnträsk), partly on paths trodden 100–200 years ago. A 600 m duckboard section crosses Källmossen bog, whose peat is over 7 m deep. A side trip leads to the historic Björnberget hill.

Four lakeside rest sites; Rudträsk is accessible for wheelchair users (car access by arrangement).
petsmo-trail.duration: From Start 1 (day care): whole trail 12.5 km, Södra Rundan 7.5 km. From Start 2 (Vikminnevägen): whole trail 11 km, Norra Rundan 7.3 km, Särkiträsk 0.3 km, Rudträsk-rundan 0.7 km.
parking_notes: Start 2 (Vikminnevägen).
Start 1 at Petsmo day care.

soderfjarden-trail.desc:
Trails on the edge of Söderfjärden, the flat cultivated basin of a c. 520-million-year-old meteorite crater. The "Skogsvägen" follows the old forest road along the forested crater edge, once the only route into Söderfjärden, past farms built where the ground was drier before the basin was drained.

The open fields are a major staging area for cranes and geese in spring and autumn.
soderfjarden-trail.duration: Loops: Östra slingan 4.7 km, Västra slingan 5.1 km, Hela slingan 8.2 km; linear Skogsvägen 5.6 km from Malax-Söderfjärdsvägen to Väster-Solf.
parking_notes: Gravel car park with map board.

ojskatsleden.desc:
Forest trail northward from Österhankmo village (Tåning) to the Öjskat area by the coast, with a lean-to midway and a grill site with benches at the far end. Towards the coast the forest turns into dry pine heath strewn with boulders and large stone blocks, and at the end of the trail the view opens over the sea.

Right by the parking area stands a memorial to the Swedish landing at Österhankmo in June 1808, during the Finnish War of 1808–1809: Swedish troops under Colonel Johan Bergenstråhle came ashore here in an attempt to retake Vaasa from the Russians, but were defeated in the Battle of Vaasa on 25 June 1808.
highlights: memorial to the 1808 Swedish landing by the parking
parking_notes: Harbour parking by Kalkmagasinet (turn at Österhankmovägen 900); walk 100 m back and 100 m north along the road to the start.

bergo-vandringsled.desc: Figure-of-eight trail on Granön in the northern part of Bergö island, in the Kvarken archipelago. It leads through the island's most scenic forest, past small lakes (Kalvskärs träsk) and rocky outcrops; the northern loop crosses Storfurusan, a ridge formerly used as a gravel pit. Duckboards cover the wettest sections. Along the way are rest areas, information boards and wooden bird and animal artworks by local artist Lars-Göran Söderholm, and the grill hut 'Adolf' with a dry toilet. Opened 2006 and re-marked 2018–19; maintained by Bergö Öråd.
bergo-vandringsled.duration: Southern loop c. 4.1 km (~1 h 20 min); northern loop c. 3.3 km (~1 h); both together c. 8 km
bergo-vandringsled.warning: Bergö is an island reached only by the free road ferry from Bredskär (crossing c. 20 min). The ferry runs to a timetable, so check the return departures before you set out to avoid being stuck on the island.
bergo-vandringsled.access: The trailhead is at Bergövägen 47 on Granön, in the north of the island. Fires are allowed only in the grill hut.
parking_notes: Free parking by the ferry landing on Bergö; the trail starts at Bergövägen 47.

majors-naturstig.desc: Loop over Majorsbacken, a forested hill with exposed rock outcrops beside Strandvägen south of Malax centre. The shortest 1.2 km loop is the rockiest, with wooden stairs on the steepest spots; the 2.2 km loop runs further south along the hillside, and both combine into the full 3.4 km round. There is a rest place with log tables. Maintained by Öjna byaförening.
parking_notes: Large parking area at the trailhead, 6 km south of Malax centre.

pixne-naturstig.desc: Nature trail starting from the centre of Malax and heading north-east into the forest between Pixne and Lillpixne. It is made of three sections that can be combined into rounds of 1.8, 3.1, 3.4 or 4.5 km; the outer part is a loop on forest paths and a forest road, while the return leg follows a sand road and the edge of the village. Built and maintained by Pixne allaktivitetsförening.
highlights: forest paths close to Malax centre
parking_notes: No trailhead parking: park at the Malax sports ground and walk c. 600 m north to the start on the light-traffic path by Klockarisvägen 14.

aminne-vandringsled.desc: Easy marked path through the forest behind Åminne village, from Mobergsvägen in the north past the Träsket area (a drained former lake bed, now forest with ditches) down to the river at Dimmornas bro, where there is a grill shelter. Loops can be made by returning along the village roads. The start can be combined with the Kvarken boat museum and Åminne bird tower. Maintained by Åminne-Tuv allaktivitetsförening.
aminne-vandringsled.duration: Marked path 2.0 km one way; 4.1 km round returning along Åminnevägen and Mobergsvägen; 5.1 km round from Åminne Folkpark
parking_notes: Roadside parking at the Dimmornas bro grill shelter, southern end of the trail; exact address uncertain.
Åminne Folkpark parking, start of the 5.1 km round; there is no parking at the northern end (Mobergsvägen).

kajane-naturstig.desc: Trail from the Kajane camp area beside a large mire near Lillträsket and Lisansjön. Duckboards lead 0.8 km across the open bog (Träskmossen) to the small lake Lillträsket, where there is a lean-to; the path then continues around and back to the camp (3.0 km), with a 0.6 km spur to the larger lake Lisansjön. Information signs present the area's animal and plant life. The camp area has a sauna, overnight cabin (fee) and barbecue shelters. Maintained by Yrkesakademin i Österbotten.
highlights: information signs on flora and fauna
kajane-naturstig.duration: Boardwalk to Lillträsket lean-to 0.8 km one way; full loop 3.0 km; spur to Lisansjön 0.6 km
kajane-naturstig.access: In 2024 only the boardwalk to Lillträsket was in usable condition; other parts of the loop may be very hard to pass.
parking_notes: Kajane camp area: from national road 8 take Kajane skogsväg (4.2 km north of the Petalax junction), drive 1.2 km, turn right, 1.4 km, then left into the area.

velkmossa-vandringsled.desc: Old forest track through the wilderness between Petalax (Malax) and Velkmossa (Närpes), mostly on the Malax side. It runs through forest and bog edges past Nojärvsträsket, a shallow, overgrown wilderness lake with reed beds that is a good breeding site for many bird species; a short spur leads to a bird tower on its shore. Another side path leads to Kackurmossen bog, and several prehistoric cairns lie near the route. Maintained by Metsähallitus (Forststyrelsen).
velkmossa-vandringsled.duration: 4.5 km one way between Viitala and Velkmoss village hall, 9 km there and back; bird-tower spur c. 0.4 km
parking_notes: Northern start with info board near the Bjurnäsvägen–Vargmossa skogsväg junction.
Velkmoss village hall (byagård), c. 0.5 km east of the southern trail end; exact address uncertain.

mamrestigen-storsjostigen.desc: Historic connecting path between the forest villages of Storsjö in Malax and Mamrelund in Petalax. It crosses a low-lying forest landscape with bogs and ditched peatland (e.g. Gorrmossen) and small rocky rises; there are prehistoric cairns near Storsjö. Maintained by Petalax hembygdsförening, Malax museiförening and private landowners.
mamrestigen-storsjostigen.duration: c. 3.5–4 km one way, 8 km there and back
parking_notes: Western start at Mamrelund; exact address uncertain.
Eastern start at Storsjön; exact address uncertain.

jarnaldersleden.desc: Short loop through an archaeologically interesting area with Iron Age cairns (gravrösen) and cup stones, from a settlement dated to about 200–700 AD; one is said to be 'the most beautiful cup stone in Finland'. The meadow and forest vegetation is rich. At the start there is an open chalet hut (fäbodstuga) with archaeological information and a summer cowshed with an agricultural exhibition. Maintained by Malax museiförening.
parking_notes: Trailhead parking by Storsjövägen, 8.5 km south of Malax church.

fabodstigen-molapne.desc: Cultural-history path through the forest at Pappersbruket (Bränno) in Molapne, where the people of Malax kept their summer pasture chalets (fäbodar). Signs mark the sites of 15 former herdmaids' cottages, mostly only foundations and hearth remains today; one restored cottage and cowshed are on site. Maintained by Malax museiförening.
parking_notes: Roadside parking at the start (map board): from road 8 at Långåminne drive 1.8 km towards Malax, turn left and follow the road 2.1 km to Molapne.

rajavuori-luontopolku.desc: Loop from the Rajavuori wilderness and hiking centre over Rajavuori, the highest ground in Laihia (80–90 m above sea level), through forest. About 700 m north-west of the yard stands an 8 m lookout tower with wide views; further on are the Rajavuori double lean-to (c. 1.5 km) and the Kaunissaari lean-to (c. 3.1 km), both with fireplaces and firewood delivered a few times a year. The loop is the northern start of the long-distance Kurjen kierros (Crane Trail) towards Levaneva. The centre (rentable, saunas) has a dry toilet and a lean-to in the yard.
parking_notes: Yard of the Rajavuori hiking centre, c. 12 km south of Kylänpää; the trail starts at the info board.

kurjen-kierros-rajavuori-levaneva.desc: Essentially the whole Kurjen kierros (Crane Trail) – a linear route despite 'kierros' (round) in its name – from the Rajavuori hiking centre to the Levaneva Mire Reserve on the Laihia–Kurikka border. After the forested Rajavuori area the trail crosses road 687 and the Kyrössuo bog north of the Kivi- ja Levalampi reservoir and joins the Levaneva trail. Levaneva is a large, open raised-bog landscape; the route crosses it on long duckboards and detours through forest islets and wooded mire edges. At Maalarinmaa there is a half-kota lean-to, a dry toilet and a bird tower over the mire, popular for watching bog-nesting birds. Near Peräkylä is the Särkinen open wilderness hut with tent area.
kurjen-kierros-rajavuori-levaneva.duration: Maalarinmaa parking to bird tower 0.6 km; Rajavuori–Maalarinmaa c. 14 km; Rajavuori–Peräkylä c. 24 km one way. The Levaneva trail itself (Peräkylä–Maalarinmaa and on) is 13.6 km one way. From the southern end, trails continue to Pässilä and Kalajaisjärvi (Ilmajoki), c. 30–50 km in total.
kurjen-kierros-rajavuori-levaneva.access: Linear route: arrange transport or walk out and back. Levaneva is a state nature reserve (Metsähallitus): stay on the marked trail.
kurjen-kierros-rajavuori-levaneva.season: Duckboards can be slippery in wet weather.
parking_notes: Northern start at the Rajavuori hiking centre.
Maalarinmaa parking on the Kurikka side: from road 687 turn towards the Kivi- ja Levalampi reservoir (signposted Kurjen kierros); exact address uncertain.
Peräkylä parking, southern access to Levaneva (Kurikka).

allisen-luontopolku.desc: Village trail in Jakkula maintained by Jakkulan kyläyhdistys. Info signs along the way present the local nature. At 0.7 km a viewing platform has been built on top of a large glacial erratic boulder; at 1.5 km is the well-equipped Haarrineva lean-to on the edge of the Haarrineva bog, with a fireplace, firewood shed and an outdoor toilet nearby. The path ends at prehistoric cairn graves (röykkiöhaudat) 1.9 km from the start.
highlights: viewing platform on a glacial erratic
allisen-luontopolku.duration: Viewpoint 0.7 km, Haarrineva lean-to 1.5 km, cairn graves 1.9 km; 3.8 km there and back
parking_notes: Trailhead with info board on Allisentie, next to the Jakkula shooting range.

isokyro-lymmyys-nature-trail.desc: A short educational loop on the sandy Hietakangas heath beside Palhojaistentie. The path crosses several forest types, from dry pine heath (kuiva kangasmetsä) to spruce and birch stands and the edge of a mire; information boards along the way present the local trees, berries (bilberry, lingonberry), animals such as squirrel, elk and wood ants, and bogs. It suits families with small children. The walk ends at a roofed kota and a log lean-to by the parking area.
parking_notes: Gravel road off Palhojaistentie at no. 260 to the kota parking area.

isokyro-fatisaari.desc: The first part winds through varied forest, after which the trail opens onto a wide treeless bog crossed on more than a kilometre of duckboards. The destination is Fatisaari, a rugged bedrock 'island' rising out of the mire, with a lean-to on top of the rock. You return the same way.
isokyro-fatisaari.duration: 1.5-2 h there and back (3.5 km each way)
parking_notes: Follow Marjoniementie to Tuurala hunting lodge, then the narrow road to the right to its end; do not park in the hunting lodge yard.

isokyro-ruusupuro-rookki.desc: Starting from the well-equipped Ruusupuro swimming beach, the loop climbs through dense, rugged forest onto bare rocky hilltops. The terrain alternates between rock, forest and steeper sections, which makes it the most varied and physically demanding of the shorter Isokyrö trails. Midway there is the Röökki lean-to and fire site; bird nest boxes have been put up along the path nearby, so birds can be watched at close range. A swim at the beach can round off the walk.
parking_notes: Ruusupuro swimming beach parking; signposted trail start.

isokyro-vuoressalo.desc: Vuoressalo is a bedrock hill rising from the flat fields of the Kyrönjoki valley. Two loops lead up onto its open, lichen-white rock outcrops with wide views. Among the rocks are curious stone formations whose human origin has long been debated, among them a 'pakouuni' (refuge oven), said to be a low wall built by peasants in the Club War (a peasant rebellion of 1596–97), where a natural cleft forms a vault about 2 m high. A lean-to lies at the south end, reached by a short spur from the red-and-white marked path. One of the 'Tarinapolku' mobile-game stories is located here.
parking_notes: Parking area across the road from the trail start; do not park on the road.

isokyro-orisberg-kotilammi.desc: The loop circles Kotilammi, regarded as Finland's oldest artificial lake - a reservoir dammed for the Orisberg ironworks - through varied terrain on forest paths, duckboards and forest roads. It starts at the bell tower of Orisberg church. Practically nothing remains of the ironworks itself, and Orisberg manor, linked with Zachris Topelius and Jean Sibelius (by tradition Sibelius and Aino Järnefelt got engaged here), is private property and not open to visitors; of the historic milieu, essentially only the church with its bell tower and the cemetery are accessible. A kota stands by the lake. Long enough to require good fitness.
highlights: Kotilammi reservoir (oldest artificial lake in Finland)
Orisberg church, bell tower and cemetery
isokyro-orisberg-kotilammi.duration: 2.5-3 h; shorter option: walk to the Kotilammi kota and back the same way
parking_notes: Parking on Åbergintie; start at the Orisberg church bell tower (during summer camps, join the trail directly from Åbergintie rather than at the camp centre).

isokyro-tuomaanmaki.desc: A varied loop through the Tuomaanmäki nature reserve, a forested hill with abundant natural values and a well-preserved Bronze Age cairn site. Several burial cairns have been dug into and robbed of stones; one has only its ring of kerb stones left, locally called the 'court stones' or 'judge's circle', which gave the hill its old name Tuomarmäki. The route also passes a rock basin that looks like a giant's kettle (but is not one) and a lean-to. One of the 'Tarinapolku' mobile-game stories is located here.
parking_notes: Park only in the parking area and do not block the trail entrance.

isokyro-lapinmaki.desc: A short, easy forest loop right at the edge of Isokyrö centre, starting beside the Lapinmäki playground. Despite the location it offers a genuine woodland walk; an optional out-and-back spur leads to the Isohaankallio rock outcrop. Good for families with children.
parking_notes: Parking at the end of Pohjantie next to the Lapinmäki playground.

isokyro-peippoonen.desc: A small network of forest paths right next to the Peippoonen residential area, combining a marked nature trail, the sawdust-surfaced Kylkkälä exercise track (ski track in winter - do not walk on it) and paths formed naturally in the woods. The terrain is varied woodland. A fire site lies along the nature trail and a kota stands next to the exercise track. Ticks are abundant in summer.
isokyro-peippoonen.network_note: Nature trail loop (~3 km, walk clockwise) plus the Kylkkälä sawdust exercise track, an old exercise track and informal paths; about 6.5 km if you walk every path.
isokyro-peippoonen.season: Many ticks in summer; exercise track is a ski track in winter.
parking_notes: Parking by the disc golf course / Kylkkälä exercise track, left just after the playground; the nature trail starts ~200 m up the pedestrian way across the road.

isokyro-ylipaa-marjamaki.desc: A hilly outdoor area of forested moraine and rock around Marjamäki, with several marked loops - largely the area's exercise tracks (snow-made ski tracks in winter, when walking on them is forbidden) - plus paths leading up from the Lukkuhaka camping area through woods. At the top of Marjamäki stand a lookout tower and two lean-tos; a further lean-to with a sledging hill is by the stadium near the youth association hall. There is an 18-hole disc golf course beside the track.
isokyro-ylipaa-marjamaki.network_note: Several loops of 1–5 km (exercise tracks of 1.4, 2, 3 and 5 km plus paths) on Marjamäki hill; about 7 km of paths in all.
isokyro-ylipaa-marjamaki.season: In winter the tracks are groomed ski tracks - no walking on them.
parking_notes: Ylipää youth association hall (Nuorisoseura) parking.
Alternative start beside the Lukkuhaka camping area; exact address uncertain.

vora-andkil.desc: Two loops through the forested hills west of Rejpelt. The long loop first climbs over bare rock slabs and boulder ground on Kondivor (Höstklint) - the trail's highest point is 52 m above sea level - then continues south through the extensive Västerskogen forest with small bog pools, mire edges and open patches before returning along the eastern side. On the later part, signs give old dialect place names derived from local legends. The short 1.7 km loop circles Kondivor hill only.
highlights: bedrock slabs and boulders on Kondivor
vora-andkil.duration: short loop ~30 min, long loop 2.5-3 h
parking_notes: Roadside parking by the start sign at the end of Kondivorvägen near Nybo.

vora-arvidsstigen-vernersstigen.desc:
Two short loops in the small hilly woods behind the Rasmusgården farm museum at Rasmusbacken, over low moraine knolls (about 20 m a.s.l.) with mixed forest. The paths are easy and passable with a pushchair; in summer fairy-tale figures and toy animals line the trails, making them popular with families.

Rasmusbacken was the home of the Rasmus siblings. Verner Rasmus (1901–1988), a farmer, amateur musician and collector, built up the collection now shown in the Verner Rasmus museum; his brother Arvid left part of his property to the foundation that runs the site, whose home farm Arvidsgården dates from 1913. A petting farm and a café are open in summer.
parking_notes: Rasmusgården parking; the trails start behind the outbuilding at Arvidsgården.

vora-coronastigen-keskis.desc: Starting at the Keskis village hall, the trail loops over Nyåkersbergen hill and through ditched forest and small rocky knolls, partly along the old lit ski track and a forest road. The longest option heads east past the rock outcrops of Storhällorna towards the Fallmossen bog. A bench and a small grill site are along the way.
parking_notes: Keskis UF (youth association hall) parking.

vora-herrgardsleden-tottesund.desc: A trail from Tottesund manor (17th-century origins) along the shores of Rämpan bay and out onto the Bytesholmarna peninsula, mostly through shoreline deciduous and mixed forest close to the water - a land-uplift coast of the Kvarken archipelago. Two lookout spots face the sea, and the far tip, Bytesholmsudden, has a barbecue hut, fireplace and dry toilet. Information boards with quizzes present trees (Swiss pine, alder, oak) and manor history, including Sibelius' wedding at Tottesund. Tables and benches along the way.
parking_notes: Parking at Tottesund manor next to the information board; exact address uncertain.

vora-kimo-bruk-trails.desc: Trails starting from Kimo Bruk, one of Finland's oldest ironworks (founded 1703), along the Kimo river valley. The 1.5 and 3 km routes follow a wide sawdust track suitable for pushchairs and, with assistance, wheelchairs; the 8 km route is partly a rough forest path. Four rest stops with tables and benches. Afterwards you can stroll through the ironworks park and walk the stone labyrinth ('jungfrudans').
parking_notes: Start at Kimo Bruk; park up by the road (exact address uncertain).

vora-kinnkangleden.desc: Starting at the eastern edge of Oravais village, a ~2 km loop crosses the forested Skrymlorna-Kuivalainen area; the 5 km option continues east through mixed forest and boulder-strewn moraine ground to the bank of the Kimo river and back. The 1808 battle of Oravais (Finnish War) is commemorated on Slagfältsvägen: the battle memorial and the Lotta Svärd stone stand about 1.3 km south-west of the start as the crow flies, and the battlefield itself lies about 1.5–2 km away. A bench and table along the route.
parking_notes: Start at the eastern edge of Oravais village (Kimovägen); exact address uncertain.

vora-komossa-hoppamaki.desc: From the lean-to at the trailhead, the path climbs gradually over open, lichen-covered bedrock slabs and rocky pine forest to Hoppamäki, at about 71 m one of the highest points in Ostrobothnia, crowned by a lookout tower. The Auras loop continues over the bare rock hills north-west of the tower towards the shore at Nörråkern; the Haaplund loop explores the rocky forest and small mires to the north-east (Lil hällan, Haplund).
vora-komossa-hoppamaki.duration: Hoppamäki 2.5 km out-and-back; Auras 3.8 km; Haaplund 4.8 km
parking_notes: Signposted from Brännarsvägen; parking by the lean-to at the start.

vora-kovik.desc: A loop through beautiful, hilly forest terrain with rocky knolls and small mires around Kovik village. Ten numbered sites along the trail tell of memorable events, villagers' everyday life and colourful characters from the village's past. Natural resting spots along the way; making fires is forbidden.
parking_notes: Parking by the trail board, signposted from Vöråvägen.

vora-lotlax.desc: Laid out in the late 1980s and restored in 2014 by the local heritage society. From the village the path heads east past Blusibacken into forest and mire terrain, ending in a small loop around a wet hollow with ponds. About halfway there is a rest area with picnic tables; the stretch up to it is easy, but parts beyond cross difficult terrain.
parking_notes: Lotlax village hall (bygård), signposted from Lotlaxvägen.

vora-rokio-norrvalla-boberget.desc: Trails north from the Norrvalla centre through the Rökiö forests: bare rock slabs, old 'troll forest' with large spruces, mires and small lakes, and ancient remains. The Norrvalla-Boberget loop reaches the Boberget hill (lean-to and fireplace); from there the link trail runs east past Lasor träsk and an ancient monument site to the reconstructed Bronze Age houses at Vitmossen, allowing long day hikes.
highlights: link to Vitmossen Bronze Age site
vora-rokio-norrvalla-boberget.network_note: Norrvalla-Boberget-Norrvalla 7.1 km with shortcuts A 1.6, B 3.0, C 4.7 km; from Boberget a 4.5 km link continues to the Vitmossen ancient houses (Norrvalla-Vitmossen-Norrvalla 16.1 km; >20 km with the Vitmossen loops).
parking_notes: Norrvalla sports and conference centre parking, with the start signposted; more access points along the Rökiö forest road.

vora-storberget.desc: A wide, easy path circling Storberget, a low rocky hill rising above the farmland of the Vörå river valley at Rejpelt. On the hill are the Fädernegården heritage museum, a dance pavilion and the village hall. Suitable for everyone and passable with a pushchair in summer.
parking_notes: Large parking by the Storberget info map; exact address uncertain.

vora-tyrstigen.desc: From the Klemetsgårdarna heritage farm the path crosses the main road and climbs to Tyrgärdback ('Tyrjäälback'), a small rocky, wooded hill thought to be an ancient assembly and sacrificial site, possibly from the 600s, named after the Norse god Tyr. Two small loops circle the hilltop before returning the same way.
parking_notes: Klemetsgårdarna museum parking.

vora-vitmossen.desc: A loop around the Vitmossen bog through rocky forest that was a seashore in the Bronze Age, when an arm of the sea reached southern Vörå. It starts at reconstructed Stone and Bronze Age houses and passes one of Finland's older known early-Bronze-Age settlements (c. 1500-900 BC) with clear hut terraces, cairn graves including large 'crater' cairns and a cremation field, and Kluvisteinin, one of the largest glacial erratic boulders in Vörå.
parking_notes: Start at the reconstructed ancient houses; exact address uncertain.

vora-vastero.desc: A coastal trail on the western shore of Västerö, largely within state-owned protected areas of the Kvarken land-uplift coast. It follows rocky shores and sea bays and crosses old-growth forest, with views to the Mickelsörarna archipelago and the open sea. History is present too: the area was important to the Jäger movement (the S/S Equity weapons landing of 1916) and traces of past wars remain. There are open day-use huts at Mastviken and Söderskatan, a tent site, campfire sites with firewood and dry toilets.
vora-vastero.duration: Whole trail ~10–11 km one way including side branches (about 6 h).
parking_notes: Southern parking and info board at the end of Söderskatavägen, signposted from Skatavägen.
Middle parking and info board near the S/S Equity memorial (Storsandviken).

vora-skidcentrum-trail.desc: A trail network behind the Vörå ski slope (Dansarhällorna) through varied terrain with old 'troll forest' and steep rock faces. The blue loop passes a lean-to (1.3 km) and circles through Norrskogen; the red extension heads east past small mires to a rest stop and Stupet, a steep cliff viewpoint.
vora-skidcentrum-trail.duration: blue loop 5 km (lean-to at 1.3 km); red extension 2.5 km (rest stop at 2.4 km, Stupet viewpoint at 3 km)
parking_notes: Ski centre parking at the foot of the slalom slope.

vora-mickelsorarna-nature-trail.desc: A short trail on Kummelskär in the outer Mickelsörarna archipelago (nearly 300 islands), part of the Kvarken Archipelago World Heritage Site where land uplift of almost 1 cm a year keeps raising new land from the sea. The path crosses the low, rocky island and shows the remains of a 16th-century fishing camp and harbour - stone foundations of fishermen's huts now well above sea level. At the start are the nature information hut with an observation tower, a summer café, lean-to, campfire site, dry toilet and rental sauna at the former coast-guard station.
vora-mickelsorarna-nature-trail.warning: Kummelskär can only be reached by boat: your own boat (nearest harbour by car is Köklot in Korsholm, ~20 km by sea) or a summer day cruise. In summer 2026 Vörå municipality arranged day cruises on M/S Filifjonkan (28.6–26.7, from Stråkaviken in Maxmo, 6–12.7 from Abborrgrund on Västerö; departs 10:00, back about 17:00; advance booking). Regular tours have not been run every year and arrangements may change – check the current situation on the Vörå municipality website (https://www.vora.fi/en/visitvora/activities/worldheritagesite/). On a cruise, be at the harbour on time: it is the only scheduled way back.
vora-mickelsorarna-nature-trail.access: No road access; the trail starts at the nature station harbour on Kummelskär.
vora-mickelsorarna-nature-trail.season: Bird nesting season 1.5-15.7: stay on marked trails. Nature hut, tower and café open in summer only.
parking_notes: Park at the departure harbour: Stråkaviken (Maxmo) for the day cruise (2026), or Köklot (Korsholm) for own boats.

vora-kimo-river-mouth-bird-towers.desc: Two birdwatching towers at the mouth of the Kimo river where it enters the shallow Oravaisfjärden bay, reached by a forest track and path of under a kilometre. The shallow, sheltered river-mouth bay on this land-uplift coast is a good spot for watching waterbirds, especially during migration.
parking_notes: Where the forest track to the towers leaves Karlebyvägen, near the Pärtstugan museum; exact address uncertain.
